chapter: Boston childhood, learning music and first gigs
title: First gigs: a five-dollar dance and the stranded Watson show
summary: A first gig had a pianist who knew only two keys; then a singer Watson's show band collapsed in Leominster and left them stranded overnight.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Now, there was a time when you went to a dance, or you were actually offered a job for five dollars.
Oh, that could have been anywhere.
That was early. That was one of your first gigs. And you mentioned that you could only play in a couple of keys.
Holmes (10/9) - 35
Me.
Yeah.
Yeah. Well, the piano player could only play in a couple of keys.
Yeah. They were E-flat...
E-flat and B-flat.
So that job came easy to you.

Yeah. Now, one time I was offered a job with a show. I forget what the girl's first name was. The last name was Watson. She was a singer, and she wanted this band on her show. She would be the leader of the band. Her name was Watson... I can't remember her first name. But she was a nice-looking girl. And she did a lot of work over in Europe somewhere.

Well, we got the band together, and got some good musicians from Boston, between Boston and Providence. We had this fellow from Providence named Smitty; he wrote this number with Erskine Hawkins' band, what's the name...
"Tuxedo Junction"?
"Steppin' In"? [ED: "Tippin' Ih" by Bobby Smith]
"Steppin' In"?
"Steppin' In was the name of it?
I don't know.
Holmes (10/9) - 36
[SINGS] That was one of Erskine Hawkins' big hits. What was his name? Smitty... Always called him Smitty. He was a drummer. He was not a saxophone player at that time, when he was with the show.
Did he play the drums with Erskine Hawkins later on?

No, he was a saxophone player with Erskine Hawkins. He was drumming with this show. And he got me on the show, in the band... And we left Boston, and we went to a little town, Limister(?), Mass. -- that was to be our first engagement. And we get to Limister, and I don't know what happened -- we didn't put on no show. The theatre didn't open or something. And there we were, stranded, forty miles from home. And we were stranded. Ain't nobody had no money. And we didn't have cars in them days.

We sat up in the theatre, in the dressing room all night, and played cards, waiting for daylight. And daylight come, one of the fellows called his mother in Boston and told her what had happened, and they drove to this town, Limister(?), Mass., and picked up some of the band and brought them back to Boston. I was one of the some of them. And that's how I got back to Boston.

That was my first what you'd call road engagement. We didn't even make one day! We got stuck there, and... Old Smitty. He was in the band And another fellow named Ford
Holmes (10/9) - 37

played piano, who was a great pianist, but... Smitty and Ford were from Providence. And all Smitty could talk about was Hilton Jefferson -- because he was from Providence, too. To Smitty, Hilton Jefferson was the world's greatest saxophonist. Which he was a damn good saxophone player. But see, Jeff was a pretty damn good saxophone player. But all Smitty would talk about was Hilton Jefferson, Hilton Jefferson...
